title: Sample stability of the measurand potassium
summary: Potassium is one of the most commonly requested laboratory tests. It plays a crucial role, for example, in the diagnosis of cardiac arrhythmias, in follow-up examinations for chronic kidney disease, and in certain drug therapies involving antihypertensive medications. Even slight deviations in blood potassium levels require medical treatment. Therefore, it is particularly important that potassium levels are measured with a high degree of accuracy. However, there are many causes for a falsely altered potassium concentration in the blood sample. Errors that occur prior to the measurement play a particularly significant role here. For example, a falsely high potassium concentration can occur if the sample is taken from an unsuitable sample material or centrifuged too late. Therefore, with this study, we aim to investigate the influence of various factors on the stability of potassium concentration and identify opportunities for improvement.
